question: What should an admitted student do if they haven't passed the Korean standard?
required_facts: ERICA lets students who took a leave of absence right after admission return once they meet the Korean requirement
New students must show TOPIK Level 3 or higher or Hanyang IIE Level 3 or higher
What an admitted student must do before that (leave placement, tuition) is not described for ERICA

inapplicable_evidence.why: Seoul undergraduate acceptance guideline (Korean Standard Fail); gold persona is at ERICA

reference_answer: At ERICA, a new student who took a leave of absence right after admission can return to school once the Korean requirement is met: TOPIK Level 3 or higher, or Level 3 or higher at the Hanyang IIE (Level 5 for the Department of Architecture). The snapshot has no ERICA acceptance guideline that says what to do before then, so confirm the steps with the ERICA OIA.
notes: Campus is not stated, and only Seoul has an explicit acceptance guideline for Korean-standard fail (guide 2751c7a0); I treat the ERICA persona as gold and use the ERICA return-to-school guide (latest, 2026 fall) as partial evidence (open question 10.4.1). Seoul spans are inapplicable. Borderline partial vs unanswerable.

question: Which insurance do I join before I start classes?
required_facts: University insurance and National Health Insurance differ by campus
At ERICA the university group insurance premium (KRW 25,000) is billed with tuition
At ERICA the National Health Insurance notice is mailed to the address on the Alien Registration Card

inapplicable_evidence.why: Seoul branch: private insurance paid by Hanyang; gold persona is at ERICA

reference_answer: It depends on your campus. At ERICA you join the university group insurance (KRW 25,000, added to your tuition bill) and also National Health Insurance, whose notice is mailed to the address on your Alien Registration Card. At Seoul the university runs a private insurance paid by Hanyang for enrolled students, plus National Health Insurance.
notes: Campus unstated; both campuses have differing university-insurance evidence, so campus is a branch (8.3, two branches). Seoul spans are listed as inapplicable (other-campus branch of the conditional answer). NHI itself is national.

question: Can I work part time while studying Korean?
required_facts: Language-training students who meet the Korean standard (TOPIK Level 2) may work up to 20 hours a week
Without the Korean standard the limit is 10 hours a week

inapplicable_evidence.why: ERICA eligibility text covers D-2 degree students; language-training (D-4) is not described

reference_answer: Yes, with a part-time permit. If you meet the Korean standard for language training (TOPIK Level 2) you may work up to 20 hours a week; if you do not, the limit is 10 hours.
notes: Only the Seoul-hosted permit form states hours for language-training students (national immigration rule); the ERICA Visa page describes D-2 degree students only. Conflict with ERICA tables for degree students is open question 10.4.4. Campus not stated.

question: Can a language-program student get the TOPIK scholarship?
required_facts: The ERICA TOPIK scholarship is for international students at ERICA whose TOPIK score is higher than the one submitted at admission or for a previous TOPIK scholarship
The ERICA page does not say whether language-program students are eligible

inapplicable_evidence.why: Seoul TOPIK scholarship exclusion; gold persona is at ERICA

reference_answer: The ERICA TOPIK scholarship goes to international students studying at ERICA whose TOPIK level has improved over the score they submitted before. The page does not say whether language-program students qualify, so ask the ERICA OIA. (The Seoul TOPIK scholarship explicitly excludes language-institute students.)
notes: Campus unstated. Seoul notice excludes language institute students, ERICA page is silent; gold persona is ERICA so the Seoul rule is inapplicable (10.4.1).

question: Does my insurance change after my visa switches from D-4 to D-2?
required_facts: Degree students pay the university group insurance (KRW 25,000) on their tuition bill
Students taking language courses should ask their language school about insurance
National Health Insurance applies to international students
reference_answer: Yes, the arrangement changes. Language-course students are told to ask their language school about insurance. Once you are a degree student at ERICA, the university group insurance (KRW 25,000) appears on your tuition bill, and National Health Insurance also applies.
notes: Only ERICA pages address language-course students, so campus is not treated as a branch (10.4.1).

question: How many hours can I work with a D-2 visa?
required_facts: Permitted hours depend on degree level, year and Korean (TOPIK) level
ERICA bachelor year 1-2 with Level 3: 30 hours on weekdays and no limit on weekends and holidays
Without the Korean level the limit is 10 hours

inapplicable_evidence.why: Seoul-hosted form with different hour limits; gold persona is at ERICA

reference_answer: Which degree level and year are you in? At ERICA a year 1-2 bachelor student who meets TOPIK Level 3 may work 30 hours on weekdays with no limit on weekends and school holidays; without that level it is 10 hours. Year 3-4 students need Level 4, and master and doctoral students have 15 or 35 hours.
notes: More than 2 branches: clarify. Campus also a branch because the Seoul-hosted form (20/25/30 h) conflicts with the ERICA table (open 10.4.4); ERICA is gold for the persona. GPA 2.0 and employer rules are caveats.

question: Which ERICA scholarship fits a second-year student with TOPIK 3?
required_facts: HIEA: undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher in the previous semester and a valid TOPIK score, tuition scholarship of 30-100%
TOPIK scholarship: KRW 1,000,000 (non-arts programs) for improving from Level 3 or lower to Level 4 or higher
reference_answer: Two ERICA scholarships fit. The Hanyang International Excellence Awards (HIEA) need an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher in the previous semester and a valid TOPIK score, and pay 30-100% of one semester of tuition. The TOPIK scholarship pays KRW 1,000,000 (non-arts programs) if your TOPIK improves from Level 3 or lower to Level 4 or higher.
notes: Program type (arts vs non-arts), GPA and the earlier-submitted score are outside the vocabulary, so they are caveats.

question: Can I apply for an outgoing program in my second year?
required_facts: Undergraduate applicants must have completed 2 to 7 semesters at the time of application
Cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 out of 4.5 is required
reference_answer: Yes, in principle. ERICA undergraduates may apply after completing 2 to 7 semesters, so a second-year student fits, provided the cumulative GPA is at least 2.5 out of 4.5 and the language score for the destination is met.
notes: Only ERICA has outgoing-program pages. The selection schedule on the page is for 2024 but the eligibility is a stable rule. Language score, double major etc. are caveats.

question: Do I need TOPIK for a part-time permit if I'm not in an English track?
required_facts: A non-English-track student must show Korean proficiency
Bachelor year 1-2: TOPIK Level 3 or higher (or KIIP Level 3 / Sejong Intermediate 1)
Bachelor year 3-4 and master: Level 4 or higher

inapplicable_evidence.why: English-track exception; student is not in an English track

reference_answer: Yes, you have to show Korean proficiency. For bachelor year 1-2 that is TOPIK Level 3 or higher (or KIIP Level 3, or King Sejong Intermediate 1); for year 3-4 and master students it is Level 4 or higher.
notes: Value changes with year/degree level (2 branches). English-track exception is inapplicable because the student says not English track. GPA 2.0 is a caveat.

question: Can I do part-time work on D-10 after finishing coursework?
required_facts: D-10 holders may work part time only under the special D-10 provisions
Requirements: changed from D-2-1~4/D-2-7, Korean degree within 3 years, TOPIK Level 4 or higher (or equivalent), no E-1~E-7 work experience
reference_answer: Only under the special D-10 provisions: you must have changed from a full-time degree or exchange visa (D-2-1~4, D-2-7) to D-10, hold a degree from an accredited Korean university earned within 3 years, hold TOPIK Level 4 or higher (or the Social Integration Program equivalent), and have no E-1~E-7 work experience. D-10-2 and D-10-3 are excluded.
notes: Whether a master student with coursework completed already holds a Korean degree is outside the vocabulary; stated as a caveat.

question: Am I eligible to change to D-10 now, or only after graduation?
required_facts: Eligibility for the D-10-1 change: legal residence, bachelor degree or higher, enough points on the job-seeker score table (or an exemption)
Whether the change is allowed now or only after graduation is not stated
reference_answer: The ERICA Visa page lists the D-10-1 conditions: legal residence in Korea, a bachelor degree or higher, and enough points on the job-seeker score table (or an exemption). It does not say whether you can apply before graduation, so ask the ERICA OIA or the immigration office.
notes: Question implies the student is still on D-2 (not D-10); gold_profile visa updated from D-10 to D-2 per 9.5. Partial with open question 10.4.3 (timing is unstated).

question: Does my health insurance change when I go from D-2 to D-10?
required_facts: Students who completed the course while residing in Korea subscribe to the university group insurance individually through the insurer website
Whether the National Health Insurance rules change when moving from D-2 to D-10 is not stated
reference_answer: The ERICA page says students who completed the course while residing in Korea must subscribe to the university group insurance individually on the insurer website. It does not say how National Health Insurance changes under D-10, so check with the National Health Insurance Corporation (1577-1000) or the ERICA OIA.
notes: Persona already holds D-10 while the question talks about the switch; left unchanged. No D-10 insurance rule exists in the snapshot.

question: Can exchange students with no TOPIK get any ERICA scholarship?
required_facts: HIEA is for regular-course students admitted through the international admission process and needs a valid TOPIK score (English track: IELTS or TOEFL)
The TOPIK scholarship only rewards a TOPIK score higher than the one submitted before
reference_answer: Not through the scholarships listed on the ERICA page. HIEA is for regular-course students admitted through the international admission process and requires a valid TOPIK score (IELTS or TOEFL for the English track), and the TOPIK scholarship only pays when your TOPIK level improves over the score you submitted before. The page lists no scholarship for exchange students.
notes: Negative claim "no exchange scholarship listed" is an inference from the page; the Seoul HIEA notices are not relevant for ERICA.

question: Can I work part time here?
required_facts: D-2 student-visa holders with a permit may work part time; D-2-8 students must wait 6 months from entry or status change
Previous-semester GPA of at least 2.0 and the Korean (or English-track) proficiency requirement
Permitted hours depend on degree level, year and Korean level
reference_answer: Which visa and degree level do you have? Part-time work needs a permit: D-2 holders qualify with a previous-semester GPA of at least 2.0 and the Korean proficiency requirement (English-track test scores count for English-track students), and D-2-8 students must wait 6 months from entry. The hours (10 to 35) depend on degree level, year and Korean level.
notes: Open questions 10.4.3 and 10.4.4: everything is unstated (visa, degree level, campus), and the Seoul form and ERICA tables disagree. I picked clarify (visa/degree level). English-track exception and GPA are caveats.

question: Which insurance rules apply to me?
required_facts: University insurance differs by campus
At ERICA: university group insurance (KRW 25,000 on the tuition bill) plus National Health Insurance at 50% of the resident premium

inapplicable_evidence.why: Seoul branch: private insurance paid by Hanyang; gold persona is at ERICA
Seoul branch: 2026 National Health Insurance premium; gold persona is at ERICA

reference_answer: It depends on your campus. At ERICA you have the university group insurance (KRW 25,000, billed with tuition) and National Health Insurance, charged at 50% of an alien resident premium. At Seoul Hanyang pays a private insurance for enrolled students and you also pay National Health Insurance (79,320 won a month from March 2026).
notes: Campus unstated, both campuses have differing evidence: campus branch (8.3). Seoul spans listed as inapplicable (other-campus branch). Exchange students: no separate rule is stated.

question: When can a graduating doctoral student switch from D-2 to D-10?
required_facts: Eligibility for the D-10-1 change: legal residence, bachelor degree or higher, points on the job-seeker score table (or an exemption)
The timing of the change relative to graduation is not stated
reference_answer: The ERICA Visa page lists who may change from D-2 to D-10-1 (legal residence, bachelor degree or higher, enough job-seeker points, or an exemption) but gives no date or timing relative to graduation. Ask the ERICA OIA or the immigration office.
notes: Borderline partial vs unanswerable (timing is the whole question; the eligibility facts are only context). Campus unstated, only ERICA has D-10 evidence.

question: Can I keep doing paid research after changing to D-10?
required_facts: D-10-1 activities cover job search and short-term internships at internship-level wages
Part-time work on D-10 is allowed only under the special provisions
Whether paid research is allowed on D-10 is not stated

inapplicable_evidence.why: Rule for D-2 students; the question is about D-10

reference_answer: The ERICA Visa page says D-10-1 covers job-search activities and short-term internships with internship-level wages, and that part-time work is allowed only under the special D-10 provisions (a Korean degree within 3 years, TOPIK Level 4 or higher, no E-1~E-7 experience). It does not mention paid research on D-10, so ask the ERICA OIA or the immigration office.
notes: Persona is still D-2 (the question is about after the change). Paid research rules in the snapshot cover D-2 only.

question: Which insurance applies after I graduate but stay in Korea?
required_facts: Students who completed the course while residing in Korea subscribe to the university group insurance individually through the insurer website
The group insurance premium is KRW 25,000
reference_answer: At ERICA, students who have completed their course and stay in Korea must subscribe to the university group insurance individually on the insurer website (premium KRW 25,000).
notes: The snapshot does not say how National Health Insurance is treated after graduation; stated as a caveat. "Graduating" persona status is not a vocabulary value for graduated students.

question: Which undergraduate admission guide is the current one?
required_facts: Download the undergraduate guide from the Admission Guideline page (Undergraduate Admission Guide Download)
The only dated undergraduate guideline in the snapshot is Spring 2021, which is outdated

inapplicable_evidence.why: Acceptance guideline for already admitted students, not the admission guide

reference_answer: Use the "Undergraduate Admission Guide Download" link on the OIA Admission Guideline page. The only dated undergraduate guideline in the snapshot is the Spring 2021 one, which is outdated.
notes: The download page does not state the cycle year, so "current" cannot be verified from the snapshot; borderline answerable vs partial. The 2026 fall document is an acceptance guideline for admitted students, not the admission guide. Only Seoul has evidence.

question: I start this fall. Which orientation file should I read?
required_facts: Read the 2026-2 (fall 2026) international student orientation materials posted on 2026-08-26
Orientation was held on 25 August 2026; hard copies are at the International Admissions Team, Room 218, Building 108
reference_answer: Read the fall 2026 (2026-2) international student orientation materials announced on 26 August 2026 on the OIA notice board. The orientation was held on 25 August 2026, and printed booklets are at the International Admissions Team (Room 218, building 108).

Applications ran from 22 to 26 June 2026

Deadline: Sunday, September 13, 2026

The university private insurance is paid by Hanyang for enrolled students

required_facts: The latest Seoul re-registration notice in the snapshot is for 2026-1 (January 2026)
No 2026-2 return-to-school notice for Seoul is available

required_facts: The 2021 notice is superseded by later entry-report notices (2022); its 2021-09-22 deadline has passed
The entry and exit report on HY-IN must be answered every semester and is mandatory for all foreign students
